text:
## Recommendation

Product effort should prioritize **billing** next quarter, specifically `billing.features_locked_behind_premium`, which has 4490 complaints [C05] and a priority score of 13442 [C08]. This is the largest named, specific issue (behind only the unplaceable `other.general` catch-all), with a mean severity of 2.993764 [C07] indicating real user frustration over lost free functionality.

## Evidence

- **billing.features_locked_behind_premium**: 4490 complaints [C05], severity sum 13442 [C06], mean severity 2.993764 [C07], priority score 13442 [C08]. Customers describe previously free features (skip, seek, playlist playback) now requiring Premium. Example: review a0d2ccd3-ebb3-46b9-bbf7-212bb0ec8e84 states "I can only 6 skip 6 stacks per hour now I can't play a song which i searched up everything is removed you need premium to do anything I am planning on switching to yt music instead of this now" — showing cancellation intent tied directly to this issue. Review 33a171b5-b930-48c3-8560-97b8deb538be: "I wish I could give this app minus stars, it has started charging money for even playing the playlist normally."

- **usability.ad_frequency**: 5488 complaints [C09], severity sum 11849 [C10], mean severity 2.159074 [C11], priority score 11849 [C12]. This is the single largest named specific issue by volume, but its mean severity [C11] is lower than billing's [C07], and example quotes attached to this issue_id in the data (e.g., 08a1f178-3e7a-4d65-9da3-dee293dd0061: "Today I almost got into an accident because of unexpected loud ad music") suggest the labeled examples don't cleanly match the ad-frequency definition, warranting caution before treating this as the top priority.

- **other.general**: 14039 complaints [C01], severity sum 28433 [C02], priority score 28433 [C04] — the largest bucket overall, but by definition it is a catch-all with no specific, placeable defect, so it cannot directly drive a product fix. Example: review 0077f010-0436-4a94-abaf-50782a8c0f16: "Very bad this application wasted my important time ,time consuming,causes illness."

## Alternatives considered

- **Access**: topic-level data shows 1610 complaints [F22] and severity sum 6291 [F23] — the smallest of the named topics among access/usability/playback/billing. No issue-level breakdown is provided here, making it a lower priority this quarter absent more specific issue data.

- **Usability**: topic-level complaints are 13163 [F14] with severity sum 33278 [F15], the highest topic total among the four candidates. Within usability, the leading specific issues are `usability.ad_frequency` (5488 complaints [C09], priority score 11849 [C12]), `usability.general` (1862 complaints [C13], priority score 4859 [C16]), `usability.playback_controls_limited` (1592 complaints [C17], priority score 4797 [C20]), `usability.shuffle_control` (1679 complaints [C21], priority score 4787 [C24]), and `usability.queue_playlist_management` (1357 complaints [C25], priority score 4121 [C28]). Usability's total volume is high, but it's spread across many smaller issues rather than concentrated in one defect, whereas billing's top issue is both large and high-severity.

- **Playback**: topic complaints are 5615 [F20], severity sum 18451 [F21]. The leading specific issue, `playback.app_crashes_freezes`, has 1160 complaints [C29] and the highest mean severity of any issue reviewed here, 3.501724 [C31], with priority score 4062 [C32]. This is a strong secondary candidate — if crash/freeze volume grows or severity data is refined, it could justify reprioritization.

- **Billing (overall)**: topic complaints 6875 [F18], severity sum 20158 [F19] — second-highest topic severity sum after usability, concentrated mainly in the single large `billing.features_locked_behind_premium` issue, supporting it as the top specific-issue priority.

## Limits

This analysis is based on a seeded random sample of review IDs [F00], with 560609 reviews outside the classification scope [F99] — counts describe only the classified reviews. There is no revenue, plan-tier, or confirmed churn data; cancellation intent (4327 reviews [F06]) is not the same as confirmed cancellation. 13974 completed reviews are flagged needs_review [F07] and are included in every count and ranking above; the flag only marks them for human inspection, not exclusion. Some classifications may be incomplete or quarantined (13 for empty text [F03], 0 for other failures [F04]). Verification agreement (topic agreement 84.6% [F11], intent agreement 91.2% [F12], severity mean absolute difference 0.155 [F13]) reflects agreement between two models on a 1000-review sample [F10], not ground-truth accuracy.
